description: #3830 — READ-command differential over the three page-alias readers: `get_page_aliases`, `resolve_page_by_alias`, `list_page_aliases_by_prefix`. All three were waived as "page-alias table outside the conformance snapshot scope" until a fixture could put the same rows on both stacks; `seed.page_aliases` is that, each `(page_id, alias)` pair inserted verbatim into the backend `page_aliases` table and appended, in fixture order, to the mock's `pageAliases` map. The alias column is `COLLATE NOCASE`, and the seed is shaped to make that collation discriminate on every read: S1's aliases are seeded as `planning-notes`, `Roadmap`, `plan` so `get_page_aliases`'s `ORDER BY alias` answers `plan`, `planning-notes`, `Roadmap` — insertion order and a byte-order (uppercase-first) sort each redden; `Roadmap` is stored capitalized and queried as `roadmap` / `road`, and the substring steps query `Plan` against lowercase `plan` aliases, so a case-sensitive equality or `includes` reddens too. `list_page_aliases_by_prefix` is `ORDER BY length(alias), alias LIMIT ?`: the four live substring matches have lengths 4, 8, 8 and 14 with the two eights an alphabetical pair, so a mock sorting alphabetically first, or one that only matched a leading prefix (`Backplan` is a mid-string hit), differs; the `limit: 2` step pins the cap below the match count. The one op soft-deletes S3, whose alias `old-plan` would otherwise be the shortest-but-one match: `resolve` misses it and the listing skips it (`b.deleted_at IS NULL`), while `get_page_aliases` on the tombstone still lists it, because only a purge cascades alias rows. That tombstone is an OP rather than seed state because a seed block cannot carry `deleted_at`. The mock's divergences this fixture found and fixed: `get_page_aliases` answered insertion order; `resolve_page_by_alias` served a tombstoned page. NOT pinned: a foreign-space exclusion — every seed block is stamped into the one harness space and no fixture section can register a second, so the active-scope steps pin only that the in-space page passes the filter; `Global` is pinned on the same data. That is also why the same PR's move of both scoped readers off the retired `block_properties(key='space')` row onto `blocks.space_id` (#3081) is aligned by inspection, not by a step: the mock dual-writes both, so no fixture can tell them apart. Also not pinned here: the out-of-range `limit` refusal (`safeLimit` keeps callers inside the cap). The writer that fills this table, `set_page_aliases`, is pinned by `page_alias_writes` (#5057).
name: query_page_aliases

queries.comment: `plan`, `planning-notes`, `Roadmap`: `ORDER BY alias` under the column's NOCASE collation. The seed lists them as `planning-notes`, `Roadmap`, `plan`, so insertion order reddens; a byte-order sort puts the capital `Roadmap` first and reddens too.
queries.name: aliases_sorted_nocase

queries.comment: S3 is soft-deleted by the op, and its `old-plan` row is still there: `get_page_aliases` reads the table without joining `blocks`, and only a purge cascades alias rows. A mock that dropped aliases on soft delete answers nothing here.
queries.name: aliases_of_tombstoned_page_survive

queries.comment: S4 has no alias rows, so the answer is an empty list — not a refusal. Empty on purpose; non-vacuous because the two steps above serve rows through the same command.
queries.name: aliases_of_page_with_none

queries.comment: `roadmap` finds the alias stored as `Roadmap` (`COLLATE NOCASE`) and answers S1 with its title. Under the active scope, so the in-space page passes the `b.space_id` filter — a mock reading membership from somewhere the seed never wrote answers null.
queries.name: resolve_case_folded_active

queries.comment: `Global` applies no space filter and finds the same page through a different alias. Pinned on the same data as the active step because the seed cannot express a second space.
queries.name: resolve_global_scope

queries.comment: `old-plan` is still an alias row (the step two above proves it), but its page is tombstoned and `resolve` joins `blocks` with `b.deleted_at IS NULL`: a miss, answered `None`. The mock served the tombstone here, which is the divergence this step found.
queries.name: resolve_tombstoned_page_misses

queries.comment: No page carries `nothing`: `None`, zero rows, not a refusal. The other negative next to the tombstone miss above; non-vacuous because the two hit steps serve rows through the same command.
queries.name: resolve_unknown_alias_misses

queries.comment: Substring, case-insensitive: capital `Plan` matches the lowercase `plan` aliases, and `Backplan` matches mid-string. `plan` (4), then the two eights alphabetically — `Backplan` before `plan-two` — then `planning-notes` (14): `ORDER BY length(alias), alias`. An alphabetical-first sort puts `Backplan` at the top and reddens; a prefix-only match drops `Backplan`. S3's `old-plan` (8) is absent: its page is tombstoned. `proj` and `Roadmap` do not match.
queries.name: prefix_shortest_first_then_alpha

queries.comment: The same four matches capped at two: `plan`, `Backplan` — the cap applies after the sort, so it is the two SHORTEST, not the first two seeded.
queries.name: prefix_limit_below_match_count

queries.comment: `road` matches the alias stored as `Roadmap` under `Global`: the LIKE is case-insensitive in the other direction too (lowercase query, capitalized row), and the unscoped branch answers the same rows the seed's one space holds.
queries.name: prefix_global_scope_case_folded

queries.comment: `ORDER BY alias` under the column's NOCASE collation, on seven aliases picked so BOTH halves of that collation are load-bearing. NOCASE folds `A`-`Z` and NOTHING else, then memcmps UTF-8 BYTES. So: `q-Öl` (`C3 96`) before `q-äl` (`C3 A4`), `Zebra` folded to `z` (`7A`) before both umlauts, `Öl` before `ärger`, and the halfwidth katakana `ｱ` (`EF BD B1`) before the apple `🍎` (`F0 9F 8D 8E`). A `toLowerCase()` fold turns `Ö` into `ö` (`C3 B6`) and REVERSES both Ö/ä pairs; a UTF-16 code-unit compare puts the apple's leading surrogate `D83C` below `FF71` and REVERSES the katakana/apple pair. The seed order is `ärger, Öl, Zebra, q-Öl, q-äl, ｱ, 🍎`, which is none of the three, so dropping the sort reddens too.
queries.name: aliases_nocase_folds_ascii_only_then_memcmps_utf8

queries.comment: `UNIQUE(alias COLLATE NOCASE)` folds ASCII only, so `Ärger` (S6) and `ärger` (S5) are two rows, and `= 'Ärger' COLLATE NOCASE` reaches exactly one of them. S5 is seeded FIRST, so a resolver that folds through `toLowerCase` merges the pair and answers S5 with the wrong title.
queries.name: resolve_ascii_fold_keeps_the_two_umlaut_spellings_apart

queries.comment: The other arm of the pair above, so neither spelling is pinned alone: `ärger` answers S5. Both arms matter — a resolver that answered S5 for everything would pass this one and fail the step above.
queries.name: resolve_reaches_the_lower_spelling_through_its_own_row

queries.comment: `LIKE '%Ärg%' COLLATE NOCASE` folds `A`-`Z` only, so the capital-Ä query reaches S6's `Ärger` and NOT S5's `ärger`. A `toLowerCase` fold answers both rows.
queries.name: prefix_ascii_fold_reaches_one_spelling_at_a_time

queries.comment: The lowercase arm: S5's `ärger` alone. Paired with the step above so neither arm is a half-covered match.
queries.name: prefix_lower_spelling_is_the_other_arm

queries.comment: `ORDER BY length(alias), alias` — two four-character aliases, so the length key ties and the tiebreak IS the NOCASE collation: `q-Öl` (`C3 96`) before `q-äl` (`C3 A4`). A `toLowerCase` fold makes it `q-öl` (`C3 B6`) and answers the other order. Deliberately ASCII-lengthed: `length()` counts characters in SQLite and UTF-16 units in JS, so an astral alias here would redden on the LENGTH key instead of the collation.
queries.name: prefix_length_tie_breaks_on_the_nocase_collation

queries.comment: `ORDER BY length(pa.alias), pa.alias` — and SQLite's `length()` counts CHARACTERS, not UTF-16 code units. `z-🍎` is THREE characters and four units; `z-ab` is four and four. So the length key separates them for SQLite and TIES them for a `String.length` mock, which then falls to the NOCASE compare and puts `z-ab` first. Unlike the `q-` pair above, this one deliberately confounds length with collation, because the length key is what it exists to pin. Seed order is `z-ab, z-🍎`, i.e. the wrong answer, so a handler that dropped the sort reddens too.
queries.name: prefix_length_counts_characters_not_code_units
